newsitem.title: UK: Iraq leads 220k bpd OPEC output rise in April - IEA.
newsitem.headline: Iraq leads 220k bpd OPEC output rise in April - IEA.

text.p: OPEC crude oil output in April rose 220,000 bpd from March to 27.13 million barrels per day (bpd), the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
A substantial increase in Iraqi output and downward revisions to March estimates accounted for much of the increase, the IEA said.

"The largest monthly gains in April occurred in Iraq, Iran, Nigeria and Indonesia, but the growth in the latter three was primarily a result of downward revisions for March," the Paris-based agency said.
"Iraqi production is assumed to have risen to 1.270 million bpd in April from 1.165 million bod in March," it said.
But the agency saw little prospect of a significant increase in Iraqi production in May or early June as the second 90-day period of the United Nations oil-for-food exchange draws to a close.

"Despite a several dollar decline since the beginning of the year, at current prices Iraq would need to produce only about 1.2 million bpd during May and the first week of June to reach the ($1 billion) target for the second 90 days," it said.

Nigeria managed to increase output by 60,000 bpd despite continued unrest in the Rivers State, with lost production on the Bonny and Forcados stream partially compensated for by "unexpectedly large increases" in Qua Iboe and Escravos pumping rates.
